title: How Crocodiles Survived the Asteroid That Killed the Dinosaurs - Nautilus
gist: A Science Advances study led by University College London, analyzing over 7,000 fossils across 400+ species against climate models, attributes crocodilian survival of the end-Cretaceous asteroid to geographic location.

insights.claim: A Science Advances study concludes crocodilians survived the asteroid impact 65 million years ago largely because of where they lived: location, location, location.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Geographic positioning, not just traits, can determine survival through shocks.
insights.locator: the secret of crocodile success boils down to three things

insights.claim: The UCL-led team examined over 7,000 fossils and records from more than 400 pseudosuchia species and compared them with computer models of Earth's climate over 245 million years.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Large fossil datasets combined with climate modelling support the finding.
insights.locator: A team of researchers led by paleontologists
